pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK and a default of 'normal'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test checks the exact list text. src/index.js adds the label only when the priority is not normal.
The 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal filters, with ids in order.
The 'AC-4' test checks the unfiltered list in id order.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter in <strong>.
The 'AC-6' test checks a 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__. The code uses a Set and searchParams.has.

The 'AC-7' test asserts exact messages for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' for every view when the table is empty. The 'No match' state test was loosened in the last commit, but AC-7 still pins the text.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test asserts it. The config check accepts it, with tests in tests/traffic-config.test.sh.

findings.what:
Commit c975d32 ('Follow-up edits') loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe('No low-priority items.') to toBeDefined(). message() returns null when there is no

, and null is defined, so the assertion can never fail. The spec records no justification. The exact text is still asserted in the AC-7 test, but the state-table row is now weakly covered.
The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the head commit c975d32 loosened an assertion in test/priority.test.js. It also says nothing about that commit.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening, or disclose and justify it in the PR body.

findings.what: The README mentions the filter but not the '— high' / '— low' labels, the filter links or the 400 on a bad value.
findings.fix: Add a short line about the labels, the filter links and the 400.

lenses.note: The spec exists with a go. The change follows its decisions. The traffic-config-check relaxation is needed for AC-8 and is disclosed in the PR.
All 8 acceptance items have naming tests. The state table rows are covered, though the No match row was weakened late.
The last commit made a state assertion unfailable. I did not run npm test; CI runs it on every push.
The README covers the filter only.
The query is parameterized and the title is escaped. The 400 and empty-message logic is correct.
The priority input is checked against an allowlist and bound as a parameter. No injection found.
No stylesheet or client UI; the page is server-rendered HTML only, with no screenshots.
No browser was available; the page is a plain server-rendered list, and the tests check its HTML.
The 'Tests loosened: none' claim is false for the head commit.
